cards.b: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.
The ability to cope with (or meet) the demands of the environment.
All body systems working well; free from illness, injury and disease; able to do everyday tasks.
Coping with stress, controlling emotions and feeling good about yourself.
Friendship and support, needs met, having value in society and mixing with others.
E.g. an athlete who trains well but smokes or has an illness.
Illness can stop training, so fitness falls.
Reduces stress and anxiety and improves self-esteem.
Make friends, teamwork and feeling part of a group.
Stronger heart, lungs and muscles; lower risk of heart disease and obesity.
Very little physical activity; can lead to obesity and heart disease.
Being very overweight from stored excess fat.
Active, balanced diet, enough sleep, no smoking or drugs.
Ability to change direction quickly while keeping control.
Ability of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen over a long period.
The time taken to respond to a stimulus.

gaps.s: Health means physical, mental and ___ well-being.
Fitness is the ability to meet the ___ of the environment.
Being able to control emotions is part of ___ health.
Having friends and support is part of ___ health.
A lifestyle with very little activity is called ___.
Excess stored fat leading to health problems is called ___.
Illness can lead to a loss of ___.

short.q: Explain the difference between health and fitness.
short.model: Health is complete physical, mental and social well-being, whereas fitness is the ability to meet the demands of an activity.

short.q: Describe two physical benefits of exercise.
short.model: Stronger heart and lungs, and a lower risk of obesity or heart disease.

short.q: Explain how team sport can improve social health.
short.model: It allows people to make friends and feel supported and part of a group.

short.q: Give two risks of a sedentary lifestyle.
short.model: Obesity and heart disease; or weak muscles and poor mental health.

short.q: Explain why a gymnast needs flexibility.
short.model: Flexibility allows a large range of movement at joints for moves like splits and reduces injury risk.
